text:
[name]
Cambridge, MA · [email] · [phone] · [url]

CURRICULUM VITAE

APPOINTMENTS
2024–present  Postdoctoral Fellow, Department of Brain and Cognitive Sciences, Massachusetts Institute of Technology. Damon Runyon Fellowship Award holder. Laboratory of a Howard Hughes Medical Institute investigator; circuit mechanisms of flexible decision making.

EDUCATION
2019–2024  Ph.D., Neuroscience, University of Michigan. Dissertation: Thalamocortical control of evidence accumulation in the mouse. Rackham Predoctoral Fellowship (final year).
2015–2019  B.S., Biology and Mathematics, University of Rochester. Summa cum laude. Phi Beta Kappa.

FELLOWSHIPS AND AWARDS
2024–2027  Damon Runyon Fellowship Award (three years; approximately 15 awarded nationally per cycle in the basic science track)
2024  University of Michigan ProQuest Distinguished Dissertation Award (one of ten university-wide)
2023  Rackham Predoctoral Fellowship, University of Michigan
2022  Society for Neuroscience Trainee Professional Development Award
2021  Cosyne travel grant
2019  Phi Beta Kappa; summa cum laude, University of Rochester

PUBLICATIONS (citations per Google Scholar, approximately 900 total)
1. [name] et al. Thalamic gating of cortical evidence accumulation during perceptual decisions. Nature Neuroscience, 2024. First author. Approximately 190 citations.
2. [name] et al. A population code for decision confidence in mouse anterior cingulate cortex. Nature Communications, 2023. First author. Approximately 140 citations.
3. [name] et al. Cell-type-specific contributions of mediodorsal thalamus to task switching. Neuron, 2022. First author. Approximately 260 citations.
4. [name] (4th of 11 authors). A cortex-wide map of decision-related activity in the mouse. Science, 2022. Approximately 210 citations.
5. [name] et al. Optogenetic dissection of thalamocortical loops during evidence accumulation. Journal of Neuroscience, 2021. First author.
6. [name] et al. Closed-loop optogenetic perturbation with sub-millisecond latency on a low-cost microcontroller. eNeuro, 2020. First author.
7. [name] (3rd of 6 authors). Behavioral state modulates thalamic responses to sensory input. Current Biology, 2021.
8. [name] (2nd of 4 authors). History biases in rodent perceptual decisions. Journal of Neurophysiology, 2020.
Preprints: one first-author manuscript under review (2025), posted to bioRxiv.

INVITED TALKS
2025  Department of Neuroscience, Columbia University (Zuckerman Institute seminar series)
2025  Princeton Neuroscience Institute
2025  Department of Neurobiology, Harvard Medical School
2024  Center for Neural Science, New York University
2023  Cosyne main meeting, selected talk from abstracts (approximately 8% of submissions)
2022  Society for Neuroscience, nanosymposium talk

RESEARCH EXPERIENCE
Postdoctoral Fellow, MIT (Sep 2024 – present)
• Leading a project combining high-density electrophysiology (Neuropixels 2.0, about 1,500 simultaneously recorded neurons) with chemogenetic manipulation of thalamic subnuclei during a dynamic foraging task.
• Developed the lab's spike-sorting and session-alignment pipeline, used by 5 lab members; processes about 2 TB per week.
• Supervise one graduate student rotation and one undergraduate (UROP).
• Secured the Damon Runyon fellowship with a proposal on thalamic contributions to belief updating.

Graduate Student, University of Michigan (Sep 2019 – Aug 2024)
• Five first-author papers (above); established the lab's two-photon imaging rig and its analysis stack.
• Mentored four undergraduates and two rotation students; two undergraduates are co-authors.
• Taught as graduate student instructor for two terms (Introduction to Neuroscience; 70 students per section).

Undergraduate Researcher, University of Rochester (2016 – 2019)
• Honors thesis on history biases in perceptual decisions; second author on the resulting paper.

SERVICE
Reviewer: Nature Neuroscience, Neuron, eLife, Journal of Neuroscience, Cosyne (2022–present; about 20 manuscripts).
Co-organizer, Michigan Neuroscience Graduate Student Symposium, 2022 (120 attendees).
Member, Society for Neuroscience; Computational and Systems Neuroscience (Cosyne).

TECHNICAL SKILLS
High-density electrophysiology (Neuropixels), two-photon calcium imaging, optogenetics and chemogenetics, head-fixed and freely moving rodent behavior, stereotaxic surgery, Python (NumPy, PyTorch, scikit-learn), MATLAB, Kilosort, Suite2p, Bayesian and latent-variable models of behavior, high-performance computing.

REFERENCES
Available on request.
